{"id": "dfddd4d4-4d80-44d6-9279-cb91143650cd", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a classic yum \"protected multilib\" conflict \u2014 it happens when both the 64-bit and 32-bit (i686) builds of a package like glibc are installed, and a security update is only resolvable for one architecture at a time, or the two architectures drift to different versions. Let me verify the recommended fix against AWS/yum documentation before giving you steps.", "type": "text"}, {"id": "tooluse_mm4qn0F5IpPdGAyuTMPRgD", "tool_name": "verify_aws_claim", "input": {"claim": "yum error Protected multilib versions glibc resolution Amazon Linux"}, "type": "tool_use"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "da68a11e-bfe4-4167-a09f-136d9d018e48", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_mm4qn0F5IpPdGAyuTMPRgD", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Additional resources\",\"context\":\"## Fix version `GLIBC_2.25' not found issue\\n\\nThis error is caused by the old version of glibc. Centralized Logging with OpenSearch with a version later than 1.2 requires glibc-2.25 or above. So you must upgrade the existing version in EC2 first. The upgrade command for different kinds of OS is shown as follows:\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nWe strongly recommend you run the commands with environments first. Any upgrade failure may cause severe loss.\\n\\n**Redhat 7.9**\\n\\nFor Redhat 7.9, the whole process will take about 2 hours, and at least 10 GB storage is needed.\\n\\n```\\n# install library\\nyum install -y gcc gcc-c++ m4 python3 bison fontconfig-devel libXpm-devel texinfo bzip2 wget\\necho /usr/local/lib >> /etc/ld.so.conf\\n\\n# create tmp directory\\nmkdir -p /tmp/library\\ncd /tmp/library\\n\\n# install gmp-6.1.0\\nwget https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gmp/gmp-6.1.0.tar.bz2\\ntar xjvf gmp-6.1.0.tar.bz2\\ncd gmp-6.1.0\\n./configure --prefix=/usr/local\\nmake && make install\\nldconfig\\ncd ..\\n\\n# install mpfr-3.1.4\\nwget https://gcc.gnu.org/pub/gcc/infrastructure/mpfr-3.1.4.tar.bz2\\ntar xjvf mpfr-3.1.4.tar.bz2\\ncd mpfr-3.1.4\\n./configure --with-gmp=/usr/local --prefix=/usr/local\\nmake && make install\\nldconfig\\ncd ..\\n\\n# install mpc-1.0.3\\nwget https://gcc.gnu.org/pub/gcc/infrastructure/mpc-1.0.3.tar.gz\\ntar xzvf mpc-1.0.3.tar.gz\\ncd mpc-1.0.3\\n./configure --prefix=/usr/local\\nmake && make install\\nldconfig\\ncd ..\\n\\n# install gcc-9.3.0\\nwget https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gcc/gcc-9.3.0/gcc-9.3.0.tar.gz\\ntar xzvf gcc-9.3.0.tar.gz\\ncd gcc-9.3.0\\nmkdir build\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/centralized-logging-with-opensearch/additional-resources.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Why do I receive errors when I use yum or dnf on my Amazon EC2 instance that runs Amazon Linux?\",\"context\":\"Short description\\n-----------------\\n\\nTo identify the error that occurred, use the output message of the yum or dnf command that you ran on your EC2 instance.\\n\\nYou might receive one of the following error messages:\\n\\n* \\\"Connection timed out ABCD milliseconds\\\"\\n* \\\"HTTP Error 403 - Forbidden\\\"\\n* \\\"HTTP Error 407 - Proxy Authentication Required\\\"\\n* \\\"GPG verification is enabled, but GPG signature is not available\\\"\\n* \\\"Could not resolve host: abcdexyz.$awsregion.$awsdomain\\\"\\n* \\\"Resolving timed out after 5000 milliseconds\\\"\\n* \\\"Failed to download metadata for repo: Cannot prepare internal mirrorlist\\\"\\n* \\\"Error: Failed to download metadata for repo 'amazonlinux': GPG verification is enabled, but GPG signature is not available\\\"\\n* \\\"/usr/bin/python: bad interpreter: No such file or directory\\\"\\n* \\\"rpmdb: BDB0004 fop\\\\_read\\\\_meta: unexpected file type or format\\\"\\n* \\\"No package X available\\\"\\n\\nResolution\\n----------\\n\\n**Note:** AL2023 uses the **dnf** command and AL2 uses the **yum** command. AL2 reaches end of life on June 30, 2026. Make sure to [migrate to AL2023](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2/ug/prepare-for-al2023.html) before that date.\\n\\nTake the following actions based on the error message that you received\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-troubleshoot-yum-errors-al1-al2\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Troubleshooting hybrid nodes\",\"context\":\"### Ubuntu\\n\\n**GLIBC not found**\\n\\nIf you are using Ubuntu for your operating system and IAM Roles Anywhere for your credential provider with hybrid nodes and see an issue with GLIBC not found, you can install that dependency manually to resolve the issue.\\n\\n```\\nGLIBC_2.32 not found (required by /usr/local/bin/aws_signing_helper)\\n```\\n\\nRun the following commands to install the dependency:\\n\\n```\\nldd --version\\nsudo apt update && apt install libc6\\nsudo apt install glibc-source\\n```\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/hybrid-nodes-troubleshooting.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Checking AWS/yum docs for fixing protected multilib glibc version mismatch errors."}

(char 0-19596)\\n    - \\\"Connection timed out ABCD milliseconds\\\" (char 1489-5027)\\n    - \\\"HTTP Error 403 \u2013 Forbidden\\\" or \\\"HTTP Error 407 \u2013 Proxy Authentication Required\\\" (char 5028-10449)\\n    - \\\"GPG verification is enabled, but GPG signature is not available\\\" (char 10450-11402)\\n    - \\\"Could not resolve host\\\" (char 11403-13273)\\n    - \\\"Resolving timed out after 5000 milliseconds\\\" (char 13274-14064)\\n    - \\\"Failed to download metadata for repo - Cannot prepare internal mirrorlist\\\" (char 14065-15267)\\n    - \\\"/usr/bin/python: bad interpreter: No such file or directory\\\" (char 15268-17087)\\n    - \\\"rpmdb: BDB0004 fop\\\\_read\\\\_meta: unexpected file type or format\\\" (char 17088-18059)\\n    - \\\"No package X available\\\" (char 18060-19596)\\n\\n# Why do I receive errors when I use yum or dnf on my Amazon EC2 instance that runs Amazon Linux?\\n\\nMy Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance runs Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) or Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023). I receive errors when I use yum or dnf.\\n\\n---\\n\\nShort description\\n-----------------\\n\\nTo identify the error that occurred, use the output message of the yum or dnf command that you ran on your EC2 instance.\\n\\nYou might receive one of the following error messages:\\n\\n*   \\\"Connection timed out ABCD milliseconds\\\"\\n*   \\\"HTTP Error 403 - Forbidden\\\"\\n*   \\\"HTTP Error 407 - Proxy Authentication Required\\\"\\n*   \\\"GPG verification is enabled, but GPG signature is not available\\\"\\n*   \\\"Could not resolve host: abcdexyz.$awsregion.$awsdomain\\\"\\n*   \\\"Resolving timed out after 5000 milliseconds\\\"\\n*   \\\"Failed to download metadata for repo: Cannot prepare internal mirrorlist\\\"\\n*   \\\"Error: Failed to download metadata for repo 'amazonlinux': GPG verification is enabled, but GPG signature is not available\\\"\\n*   \\\"/usr/bin/python: bad interpreter: No such file or directory\\\"\\n*   \\\"rpmdb: BDB0004 fop\\\\_read\\\\_meta: unexpected file type or format\\\"\\n*   \\\"No package X available\\\"\\n\\nResolution\\n----------\\n\\n**Note:** AL2023 uses the **dnf** command and AL2 uses the **yum** command. AL2 reaches end of life on June 30, 2026. Make sure to [migrate to AL2023](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2/ug/prepare-for-al2023.html) before that date.\\n\\nTake the following actions based on the error message that you received.\\n\\n### \\\"Connection timed out ABCD milliseconds\\\"\\n\\n**Make sure that your instance allows outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic**\\n\\nMake sure that the instance's security group and network access control lists (network ACLs) [allow outbound traffic on ports 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS)](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/connect-http-https-ec2). Also, make sure that the network ACLs allow inbound traffic on ephemeral ports 1024-65535.\\n\\nCheck the operating system (OS) firewall rules to confirm that no roles block outbound traffic on ports 80 or 443. Run the following commands for each firewall.\\n\\niptables:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nsudo iptables -L -n\\n```\\n\\nFirewalld:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nsudo firewall-cmd --list-all\\n```\\n\\nnftables:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nsudo nft list ruleset\\n```\\n\\n**Check your network configuration settings**\\n\\nTo access Amazon Linux repositories, you must use one of the following network configurations:\\n\\n*   For an instance in a public subnet, use [an internet gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.html#vpc-igw-internet-access).  \\n    **Note:** The instance must have a public IP address or Elastic IP address.\\n*   For an instance in a private subnet, use a [NAT gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html) or a [NAT instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_NAT_Instance.html).\\n*   For an instance in a private subnet without internet access, [use an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) virtual private cloud (VPC) endpoint](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-al1-al2-update-yum-without-internet). With a VPC endpoint, you can directly reach the repository buckets.\\n*   For an instance that uses a proxy, configure yum or dnf to use the proxy. Add the following parameters to the **/etc/yum.conf** file for AL2 instances and the **/etc/dnf/dnf.conf** file for AL2023 instances:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    proxy=http://proxy-server-IP-address:proxy_port\\n    proxy_username=proxy-user-name\\n    proxy_password=proxy-password\\n    ```\\n    **Note:** Replace **proxy-port** with the port that your proxy uses, **proxy-user-name** with your proxy username, and **proxy-password** with your proxy password. System-level environment variables such as **http\\\\_proxy** or **https\\\\_proxy** don't apply to yum or dnf. You must configure the proxy settings directly in the configuration file.\\n\\n**Check for issues with third-party repositories**\\n\\nAn unreachable third-party repository in **/etc/yum.repos.d/** can block all yum operations.\\n\\nTo identify the repository with issues, run the following command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nyum repolist -v\\n```\\n\\nTo temporarily deactivate the repository with issues, run the following command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nyum --disablerepo=reponame update.\\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **reponame** with the repository name.\\n\\n**Confirm that you can access the Amazon Linux repository**\\n\\nRun the following command based on your Amazon Linux version to confirm that you can reach the repository endpoint.\\n\\nAL2023:\\n\\n```plaintext\\ncurl -I al2023-repos-us-east-1-de612dc2.s3.dualstack.us-east-1.amazonaws.com\\n```\\n\\nAL2:\\n\\n```plaintext\\ncurl -I amazonlinux.us-east-1.amazonaws.com \\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **us-east-1** with your instance's AWS Region. The preceding command tests only network reachability. A **403** response confirms that the repository is reachable. The \\\"access denied\\\" error is expected because curl doesn't have repository authentication credentials. If the command times out instead, then the network path to the repository is still blocked.\\n\\n### \\\"HTTP Error 403 \u2013 Forbidden\\\" or \\\"HTTP Error 407 \u2013 Proxy Authentication Required\\\"\\n\\n**Note:** For paths that don't exist in an Amazon S3 bucket, you receive HTTP 403, not HTTP 404.\\n\\nIf your yum or dnf URL contains an incorrect path because of configuration issues, then you receive a 403 error. To troubleshoot this issue, take the following actions based on your configuration.\\n\\n**You use a VPC endpoint**\\n\\nIf you use an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint, then [make sure that the VPC endpoint policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html#edit-vpc-endpoint-policy-s3) has the required permissions. Allow **s3:GetObject** and **s3:ListBucket** on the following repository bucket Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) based on your Amazon Linux version.\\n\\nAL2023:\\n\\n**arn:aws:s3:::al2023-repos-region-de612dc2**\\n\\n**arn:aws:s3:::al2023-repos-region-de612dc2/\\\\***\\n\\nAL2:\\n\\n**arn:aws:s3:::amazonlinux-2-repos-region**\\n\\n**arn:aws:s3:::amazonlinux-2-repos-region/\\\\***\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **region** with your instance's Region. If you have instances in multiple Regions, then make sure that the VPC endpoint policy in each Region includes the required permissions.\\n\\nIf you also use an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) instance profile, then confirm that the instance's IAM role has the required permissions.\\n\\nExample permissions policy:\\n\\n```plaintext\\n{\\n  \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n  \\\"Action\\\": [\\n    \\\"s3:GetObject\\\",\\n    \\\"s3:ListBucket\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n    \\\"arn:aws:s3:::al2023-repos-region-de612dc2\\\",\\n    \\\"arn:aws:s3:::al2023-repos-region-de612dc2/*\\\"\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **region** with your instance's Region.\\n\\nFor more information, see [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html).\\n\\n**You migrated from AL2 to AL2023**\\n\\nAL2023 uses different repository bucket URLs than AL2. After you migrate, update your proxy, firewall, and VPC endpoint policies to allow traffic to the new AL2023 URLs. AL2023 uses the **al2023-repos-region-de612dc2.s3.dualstack.region.amazonaws.com** format.\\n\\n**Note:** Replace region with your Region. If your repository references **cdn.amazonlinux.com**, then the URL requires internet access. The URL doesn't work for instances in private subnets that have only a VPC endpoint. In this scenario, use the mirrorlist format. The default mirrorlist URL is **mirrorlist=https://al2023-repos-$awsregion-de612dc2.s3.dualstack.$awsregion.$awsdomain/core/mirrors/$releasever/$basearch/mirror.list**.\\n\\n**You have an incorrect release version variable**\\n\\nThe **/etc/dnf/vars/releasever** file might contain an incorrect value such as **2023** instead of the fully versioned **2023.6.20250929** format. Or, the **system-release** package might be missing. In this scenario, dnf constructs a repository URL that's not valid and you receive a \\\"403 Forbidden\\\" error for the nonexistent path.\\n\\nTo resolve this issue, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Run the following command to check the current release version:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    cat /etc/dnf/vars/releasever\\n    rpm -q system-release\\n    ```\\n    \\n2. If the **system-release** package is missing, then run the following command to set a temporary release version and reinstall the package:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    echo \\\"latest\\\" | sudo tee /etc/dnf/vars/releasever\\n    sudo dnf install system-release\\n    ```\\n    \\n3. Run the following command to remove the manually configured release version so that dnf uses the system default:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    sudo rm /etc/dnf/vars/releasever\\n    ```\\n    \\n4. (Optional) To update the repository version, run the following command:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    sudo dnf upgrade --releasever=latest\\n    ```\\n    **Important:** The preceding command allows the **system-release** package to control the version. If you manually set **/etc/dnf/vars/releasever**, then you must update the file each time that you upgrade to a later AL2023 release. You won't automatically receive security updates for newer versions. For more information about how **releasever** determines repository version, see [Using Deterministic upgrades through versioned repositories](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2023/ug/deterministic-upgrades-usage.html).\\n\\n**You use a proxy**\\n\\nIf you use a proxy to access Amazon Linux repositories, then check the following configurations:\\n\\n*   Make sure that the .**amazonaws.com** subdomain is on the allowlist in your proxy configuration.\\n*   Make sure that the proxy doesn't perform SSL/TLS inspection on traffic to AWS repository endpoints.  \\n    **Note:** Proxies that inspect SSL/TLS, such as Zscaler, can cause certificate trust failures and might block .rpm files by default.\\n*   Make sure that the proxy configuration in **/etc/yum.conf** for AL2 or **/etc/dnf/dnf.conf** for AL2023 matches your proxy settings.\\n\\nIf you receive the \\\"HTTP Error 407 \u2013 Proxy Authentication Required\\\", then confirm that the **proxy\\\\_username** and **proxy\\\\_password** values are correct \",\"total_length\":19597,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":10000,\"truncated\":true,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

**What's causing it**

"Protected multilib" errors happen when yum tries to update a 64-bit package but can't simultaneously resolve a matching update for its 32-bit (`.i686`) counterpart (or vice versa) — so you end up with mismatched versions of a package that yum considers must stay in version-lockstep across architectures (`glibc` is the classic example). It almost always means the `.i686` package is installed but isn't actually needed — most EC2 AL2 instances have no 32-bit workload, and the i686 glibc got pulled in as a dependency of something else at some point.

**How to resolve it**

1. **Check if you actually need the i686 package:**
   ```
   rpm -qa | grep glibc
   yum list installed | grep '\.i686'
   ```
   See what else is installed in i686 — if it's just glibc and its direct deps (`libgcc`, `nss-softokn-freebl`, etc.) with nothing else depending on 32-bit libraries, it's safe to remove.

2. **Remove the 32-bit package** (most common fix):
   ```
   sudo yum remove glibc-2.26-32.i686
   ```
   (Use the exact i686 package/version from your error — yum will tell you what else gets removed as a dependency; review that list.)

3. **Re-run the update:**
   ```
   sudo yum update glibc
   ```
   Now yum only needs to resolve the 64-bit version, so it should apply cleanly.

4. **If you DO need 32-bit glibc** (e.g., running a legacy 32-bit binary), instead sync both architectures manually:
   ```
   sudo yum update glibc.x86_64 glibc.i686
   ```
   forcing yum to resolve both in the same transaction, which is usually what gets stuck when only one arch is specified.

5. **If neither works**, clear yum's cache and metadata and retry — stale metadata sometimes causes yum to miscalculate protected-multilib constraints:
   ```
   sudo yum clean all
   sudo rm -rf /var/cache/yum
   sudo yum update glibc
   ```

**Recommendation:** go with step 2/3 first — removing the unused 32-bit glibc. It's the standard fix for this exact error on AL2 and resolves the version mismatch without needing to touch the 64-bit package at all.

One more thing worth flagging: AL2 reaches end of life June 30, 2026, so if this instance is sticking around, it's worth planning a migration to AL2023 (which uses `dnf` and doesn't carry this multilib legacy baggage).
